text:
The Devils were down 4-2 in the second period at UBS Arena, and they still found a way out. Jack Hughes ended it 1:18 into overtime, a wrist shot off a pass from his brother Luke, and New Jersey took a 5-4 win for its fourth straight victory. Hughes was the first player taken in the 2019 draft, and on this night he looked the part, with a goal, an assist and five shots on goal in just under 24 minutes.

The scoreboard barely hints at how lopsided the play was. New Jersey put 50 shots on Ilya Sorokin to the Islanders' 23 on Jake Allen, and the Devils piled up 5.45 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to 3.24. Our numbers say New Jersey deserved to win 80 percent of the time, meaning it took the game in four of every five simulated replays. The Islanders scored on chances worth just 5 and 7 percent, while Declan Chisholm's second-period goal for the Devils came on a 5 percent look too. Sorokin's night was better than a 4-5 line suggests: he stopped 45 of 50 and gave up only about half a goal more than the chances warranted. Luke Evangelista tied the game in the third and added an assist on Dougie Hamilton's power-play equalizer, and New Jersey's top line owned the shot quality while it was on the ice.

For the Islanders, this one stings, since they led by two and had beaten New Jersey 6-0 on Oct. 3. They also took 32 penalty minutes to the Devils' four, and New Jersey got its tying goal on one of those power plays. The Devils extend their winning streak to four, and the comeback fits the way they played: they kept pushing until the score caught up.
